confidence_interval.excerpt: Green tea intake (≥500 ml/d) was inversely associated with ccRCC risk, with an AOR of 0.34 (95% CI 0.21-0.55).

comparison.excerpt: Green tea intake (≥500 ml/d) was inversely associated with ccRCC risk

design.excerpt: We carried out a hospital-based case-control study

timing.excerpt: Between 2007 and 2009, 250 newly diagnosed, histologically confirmed ccRCC cases

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale

validated_results.title: Sugar substitutes: Health controversy over perceived benefits.
validated_results.reason: This is a narrative review of the health controversy over sugar substitutes rather than an original human study of sweetener intake and incident bladder cancer.
